newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest milling wheat marches on, maize eases.
newsitem.headline: Budapest milling wheat marches on, maize eases.

text.p: Wheat futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange continued their rise on Monday whereas maize eased on good crop expectations, traders said.
"The same quality fears that drove wheat prices higher for a week dominated today," said Dezso Kormendi of LaSalle.
Milling wheat prices rose the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for most positions, but freed-up January and March surged 1,150 and 1,280 forints, to end at 28,530 and 29,300 forints, respectively.
Grains futures prices which had taken their cue from Chicago prices until early July, have since been driven by local factors such as crop forecasts, quality estimates and weather.
Almost three weeks of rainfall have both delayed harvesting and lowered the quality of an expected high-volume wheat crop of five million tonnes.

Dry and sunny weather returned to Hungary on Sunday and with medium-term forecasts showing it was likely to stay, the Agriculture Ministry estimated wheat harvesting to be finished within eight to 10 days.

An agriculture ministry official said earlier today that the wheat already harvested -- about half of this year's crop -- had a gluten content of about 27 percent, down from an initial 30 to 32 percent.
While worries of low quality alone would not have justified a rise of feed wheat prices, the edgy market sentiment drove those up as well, Kormendi said.
Feed wheat prices rose by between 50 forints for the furthest maturity, March and 400 forints for the nearest one, August.
Feed barley prices rose by between 100 and 380 forints for the 1997 maturities in minimal turnover and prices changed more in sympathy with wheat than on any new information.

Rainfall that was bad news for wheat helped maize which was likely to yield a crop even better than last year's already good six million tonnes, and this expectation was reflected in easing maize futures prices.
Maize futures finished 50 to 190 forints lower for all but the steady August position.
Total grains futures turnover dropped to 1,006 lots or 490 million forints from Friday's 1,435 lots or 742.6 million forints.
Milling wheat gave half of the turnover in volume terms with 525 contracts.
